hero.tag: Second Language Evaluation · Levels B and C
hero.title: Practise for your SLE.
hero.lede: Palier is a free study tool for the Public Service Commission’s Second Language Evaluation. Take timed reading and written-expression drills and mock exams, get AI feedback on your writing, and rehearse the oral interview out loud with an AI partner. No account needed.

key.body: Writing feedback, generated sets and spoken practice run on your own OpenAI key. You create it at openai.com, paste it into Palier, and each feature shows its cost first.

estimate.body: Progress shows an estimate of your level with its uncertainty, and says what it rests on.

official.a: No. Palier is not the exam and is not connected to the Public Service Commission. It contains no real test questions. It gives you an estimate with its uncertainty shown, never a promised result.

account.a: No. Drills and mock exams work without one. Sync is on by default so your other devices can pick up your progress, using a random id with no name or email. You can turn it off at any time.

key.a: A personal access code from your own OpenAI account. You create it at openai.com and paste it into Palier. It lets Palier ask the AI to mark your writing and talk with you, billed to your account.

cost.q: What does the OpenAI key cost?
cost.a: Palier itself is free. Only writing feedback, generated practice sets and spoken practice use an OpenAI key, and it is your own, billed by OpenAI on your account. Each feature shows its cost before it spends anything.

source.q: Where do the questions come from?
source.a: The items are written by an AI model, Claude, as original passages and questions that copy nothing. Each one is reviewed blind by separate instances of the same model and by a set of automatic checks; an item that fails is discarded. Every item shows where it came from, and reporting one takes a single tap.

privacy.a: Palier has no server that stores your data. Your practice, API key, session audio, oral transcripts and writing submissions stay on your device. When you use an AI feature, the text or audio it needs is sent directly from your browser to OpenAI under your own key, and OpenAI’s terms and privacy policy apply to it. Palier never receives it. There are no analytics, no advertising and no tracking cookies. You can export or delete everything in one step.

close.title: Your next level starts here.
close.body: Open Palier and do today’s practice. No account, no download, free to use.

about.title: What Palier is, and what it is not
about.independence: Palier is an independent study tool, built in the open. It is not the exam, and using it is not a substitute for the Public Service Commission's own preparation material.
about.noRealItems: It contains no real test questions. Every item is written or generated for practice, and no result it produces is official.
about.what: A free, source-available place to practise the Second Language Evaluation’s reading, written expression and oral tests, aiming at level B or C. Drills and mock exams need no account and work offline. The parts that cost money (writing feedback, generated practice sets and spoken practice) run on your own OpenAI key, straight from your browser, and each one shows its cost before it spends.
about.notCourse: Not a language course. It assumes you already work in French and helps you perform under exam conditions.
about.notPredictor: Not a predictor. It gives an estimate with its uncertainty shown, never a promised result.
about.notOfficial: Not affiliated with the Public Service Commission of Canada, the Canada School of Public Service, or any department.
about.bankMachine: The items are written by an AI model, Claude, as original passages and questions in the register of the federal workplace. Nothing is copied from a real exam or a real document. No person reads every item before it is published. Each one is reviewed blind by separate instances of the same model, which must find the intended answer and no second one, and then passes a set of automatic checks. An item that fails is discarded, not repaired. Items written by people are welcome, and they pass the same checks.
about.bankHonest: So the bank tells you where each item came from. Any item’s provenance is one tap away. Reporting an item takes one tap and opens a public issue, and items that turn out badly are retired. Your estimate says what it rests on, and is never quietly adjusted.
about.who: Palier is a personal, non-governmental project, built in the open by Doug Keefe and anyone who contributes. It holds no government information and accepts none.
about.licence: The code is under the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0 and the content under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0. You may copy it, change it, and run your own version for any non-commercial purpose. Commercial use is not permitted.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: Palier keeps your practice in your browser. When sync is on, which it is unless you turn it off, a copy of your progress is also kept on Palier’s server, so your other devices can have it. This page says exactly what that copy holds, and what never leaves your device.
privacy.heldTitle: What the server holds, when sync is on
privacy.held: A random account id, a scrambled (hashed) secret for each device, your language and target settings, which milestones and streak notes you have already been shown, and a copy of your progress: your answers, your review schedule and your exam results. No name, no email, no department, no free text, and nothing that identifies you.
privacy.neverIntro: These stay on your device, under every setting:
privacy.neverServer: Nor does the server keep your IP address, beyond using it for a moment to limit abuse, and nothing links an anonymous item statistic to your account.
privacy.deletedTitle: What is deleted on a schedule
privacy.deleted: An account with no activity for 180 days is deleted from the server, with everything it holds. Anything you delete is gone from the server within 90 days.
privacy.third: OpenAI, only if you add a key: the paid features call OpenAI on your own account, under your own agreement with them. Palier’s server never keeps your key; it sees it only for a moment when you start a studio conversation, to open it with OpenAI, and not even then if you point studio mode at an endpoint of your own in the key settings. Vercel hosts the site. Nobody else.
privacy.noTracking: No analytics, no advertising, and no cookies that would need a banner. Anonymous statistics on how items perform are sent only if you say yes after a mock exam, and they are off until you do.
privacy.rights: Export everything to a file, import it back, or delete everything, on this device and on the server, in one step each. Sync can be turned off at any time, and turning it off offers to delete the server’s copy.

key.realtimeNote: OpenAI’s live voice conversations need a short-lived pass, and OpenAI makes one only for a request from a server. So when you start a studio conversation, your key goes once to Palier’s server, which uses it for that one request and passes the pass back. It is never written down, logged or kept. This is the only time your key reaches our infrastructure.

key.realtimeOwnTitle: Or have your own server ask for the pass
key.realtimeOwnIntro: If you would rather your key never reached Palier’s server, deploy the small endpoint in Palier’s repository on your own Cloudflare or Vercel account and enter its address here. When you start a studio conversation, Palier opens it in a small window and hands your key to it there, and nowhere else. Your endpoint asks OpenAI for the pass, and the window closes itself. The address stays on this device: it is never synced or exported.

key.offerUnlocks: A key turns on the parts that use AI: the diagnostic and its written result, feedback on your writing, fresh practice items written for you, and spoken practice with an examiner.
key.offerCosts: You pay OpenAI directly for what you use, and you can set a monthly limit on your OpenAI account.
key.offerStays: The key stays in this browser and goes to OpenAI, and once to Palier’s server for each studio conversation, which keeps nothing. Everything else in Palier works without one.
key.guideIntro: Five steps, on OpenAI’s site. Palier sees none of it.
key.guideStep1: Sign in to your OpenAI account, or create one, at platform.openai.com.
key.guideStep2: On the billing page, add a payment method or credit: a key only works on an account that can pay.
key.guideStep3: On the API keys page, choose “Create new secret key”. Name it Palier, so you know what it is for, then copy it: OpenAI shows it only once.
key.guideStep4: On the limits page, set a monthly budget. That limit, not Palier, is what bounds what you can spend.
key.guideStep5: Come back here and paste the key into the field on Your API key.

oral.title: Spoken practice
oral.intro: Rehearse the oral interview in one of two modes. In practice mode the examiner asks in writing and aloud, and you answer turn by turn. In studio mode you talk with the examiner live, as in the real test.
oral.practiceMode: Each answer you record is sent to OpenAI to be written down, on your key. The recording of your answers stays on this device, and nothing here is synced or exported.
oral.studioMode: Your key goes once to Palier’s server, which uses it to open the conversation with OpenAI and keeps nothing. Your voice goes to OpenAI only. The recording of your microphone stays on this device, and nothing here is synced or exported.
oral.studioModeOwn: Your key goes once to your own endpoint, in a small window Palier opens, to open the conversation with OpenAI. It never reaches Palier’s server. Your voice goes to OpenAI only. The recording of your microphone stays on this device, and nothing here is synced or exported.
